battle.name: 德克薩斯革命
battle.theater: 德克薩斯東南部與聖哈辛托河畔
battle.brief: 1835年3月起，德克薩斯移民因廢州、徵稅與調兵而武裝自衛，10月岡薩拉斯首捷，12月收復聖安東尼奧。1836年2月聖安東尼奧圍城13日陷落，3月27日古利亞德慘案震動全境，4月21日聖哈辛托一戰以18分鐘擊潰墨軍俘其總統。西班牙長槍僅存於墨軍槍騎兵長矛與堡內儀仗，獵槍才是主流。

kit.name: 長槍
kit.history: 方陣的長矛讓火槍隊站在後面。密西西比之後，長矛和火槍一起站住了。

countries: 交戰一方是德克薩斯殖民地的武裝居民，通稱德克薩斯軍或德克薩斯民兵。他們來自德國、路易斯安那與美國南部，多為德意志裔的農場主、城鎮商人與拓荒者，由各城鎮召開的公議會所授權的十三人委員會與各郡安全委員會領導，沒有常備軍，志願兵靠自備裝備與同儕名譽入伍，軍餉靠募捐與徵用，直到共和國臨時立法成立後才由公庫撥付。指揮體系極為扁平：威廉·巴雷特·特拉維斯與詹姆斯·布伊在聖安東尼奧領軍，詹姆斯·范寧在岡薩拉斯與古利亞德掌兵，山姆·休斯敦自1836年起擔任全軍總司令，另有數百名自稱分鐘民兵的自耕農擔任散兵、哨戒與後勤。另一方是墨西哥共和國的科阿韋拉－德克薩斯州政府與其正規軍：北方師與東方師的步兵、騎兵與炮兵，軍官多為克里奧爾人，士兵多為徵召的農民，訓練與裝備參差，士氣低落，且士兵普遍不願對同種族的白人作戰。墨方指揮核心是總統安東尼奧·洛佩斯·德·聖安納，戰前由州總督伊格納西奧·佩雷斯、州議會與地方軍方分掌其政，入境之後由聖安納直接坐鎮；貝克薩爾之役交由州長阿古斯丁·阿胡馬達與波利卡多·洛佩斯率軍，阿拉莫與古利亞德則由倫布雷、阿雷東多、塞斯馬、烏雷亞等將領分節制。值得一提的是德克薩斯境內的德裔特哈諾社群分裂成兩半：胡安·塞金等少數人倒向革命，多數人則被徵召進墨西哥軍隊，這使這場戰爭同時也是一場內戰。
countriesEn: One belligerent was the armed population of the Texas settlements, known as the Texian army or the Texian militia. They came from Germany, Louisiana and the southern United States and were mostly German-descended farmers, town merchants and frontiersmen. They were governed by the committees appointed by town meetings and consultations, among them the Committee of Thirteen and the local committees of safety and vigilance. There was no standing army: enlistment rested on a man's own equipment and on his standing among his neighbours, pay was raised by subscription and voluntary levy, and only once the provisional legislature of the republic existed was the army funded from the public purse. The command structure was extremely flat. William Barret Travis and James Bowie led at San Antonio, James Fannin held the command at Gonzales and at Goliad, Sam Houston became commander in chief in 1836, and several hundred ordinary settlers who enlisted as minute men served as skirmishers, pickets and baggage handlers. The other side was the government of the Mexican state of Coahuila and Texas together with the regular army of the Mexican Republic: infantry, cavalry and artillery of the Department of the North and of the Department of the East. The officers were mostly Creoles and the soldiers mostly conscripted peasants, unevenly trained, unevenly equipped and low in morale, and they were generally unwilling to fight white men of their own race. The command centre of that army was President Antonio López de Santa Anna, who had taken power after the imprisonment and exile of 1833 and 1834 and who came to Texas meaning to make a show of severity on the frontier. Before the fighting the state governor, the state assembly and the local military officers ran the machinery of government; once Santa Anna was in the field he directed operations in person, and the army was handled in sections by the governor Agustín Ahumada and Policarpo López at Béxar and by officers including Remblé, Arredondo, Sesma and Urrea at the Alamo and at Goliad. One feature deserves emphasis: the Tejano community of Texas split in two. A few men such as Juan Seguín threw in their lot with the revolution, but most Tejanos were conscripted into the Mexican army, so the war was civil war as well as invasion.
people: 安東尼奧·洛佩斯·德·聖安納是這場革命對面的主角。他1833年推翻改革派政府接管墨西哥，旋因叛亂入獄，1834年流亡得救，1835年以德克薩斯需要一場嚴厲的教訓為由重掌大權，隨即廢除科阿韋拉－德克薩斯州、加徵關稅、派遣兵團。戰事中他親率大軍越過格蘭德河，坐鎮阿拉莫圍城，下令在古利亞德槍殺降卒，最後在聖哈辛托被俘，日後在一八四五年瓦耶克雷亞斯被處決。威廉·巴雷特·特拉維斯是德克薩斯方面的戰場核心，律師出身，1835年11月自願從軍，三週內招募四十人，越過格蘭德河後迅速成軍，在貝克薩爾之役任突擊指揮，在阿拉莫守軍中擔任主將，最後死在3月6日黎明前的夜襲裡。詹姆斯·布伊是德克薩斯最早的定居者之一，與聖安納有生意往來，在貝克薩爾率眾奪回聖安東尼奧，入堡後與特拉維斯共同防守，陣亡於破曉前的最後一刻。戴維·克羅克特是田納西州的前國會議員，1835年底自納什維爾南下，據信與守軍同死於阿拉莫。詹姆斯·范寧在古利亞德被俘，3月27日與數百名戰俘一同被槍斃。山姆·休斯敦自1836年擔任全軍總司令，刻意按兵不動以免後方受襲，最後在聖哈辛托選擇開戰。斯蒂芬·奧斯汀以德克薩斯之父聞名，1835年秋赴墨西哥城談判，翌年12月病逝，未及見證革命。胡安·塞金是德克薩斯土生土長的特哈諾，先在岡薩拉斯與貝克薩爾為革命軍作戰，後轉投墨西哥軍，參與阿拉莫與聖哈辛托兩役。此外，大衛·伯內特在1835年7月草擬《人民決議》並主張召回被派往德克薩斯的舊陸軍，威廉·洛在聖哈辛托率九十人分隊奪橋斷援，班·湯普森以雙生姊妹砲聞名，喬治·金布爾率岡薩拉斯的32人突入阿拉莫，十九歲的號手阿爾馬隆·迪金森則是阿拉莫少數生還者，隨後又赴古利亞德。
peopleEn: Antonio López de Santa Anna was the principal figure on the opposing side. In 1833 he overthrew the reformist government and took charge of Mexico, was promptly imprisoned for rebellion, was exiled and returned in 1834, and in 1835 came back to power on the argument that Texas needed a severe lesson. He abolished the state of Coahuila and Texas, raised the tariffs and sent troops north. During the war he led his army across the Rio Grande in person, sat before the siege of the Alamo, ordered the prisoners at Goliad shot, and was finally taken prisoner at San Jacinto; he was executed at Puebla in 1845. William Barret Travis was the fighting core on the Texian side. A lawyer, he enlisted of his own will in November 1835, raised forty men within three weeks, and after crossing the Rio Grande had a force that grew fast; he led the assault at Béxar and commanded the garrison of the Alamo, where he died in the night attack of 6 March, in the hour before dawn. James Bowie was one of the earliest settlers of the colony and had business dealings with Santa Anna; he led the party that retook San Antonio at Béxar and shared the defence of the Alamo, falling in the last minutes before daybreak. David Crockett, a former congressman from Tennessee, came south from Nashville at the end of 1835 and is believed to have died with the garrison. James Fannin was taken at Goliad and shot with several hundred other prisoners on 27 March. Sam Houston, commander in chief from 1836, deliberately kept his army still so that it would not be pinned in the rear, and chose to fight at San Jacinto. Stephen F. Austin, known as the father of Texas, went to Mexico City to negotiate in the autumn of 1835 and died of illness in the following December, not living to see the revolution. Juan Seguín was a Texan-born Tejano who fought for the revolution at Gonzales and at Béxar and then went over to the Mexican army, taking part in the Alamo and at San Jacinto. Among the rest, David G. Burnet drafted the Resolves of the People of Texas in July 1835 and argued for the recall of the old garrison troops, William Law led the ninety men who seized the bridge at Vince's Bayou, Ben Thompson is remembered for the Twin Sisters, George C. Kimble led the Thirty-Two of Gonzales into the Alamo, and Almaron Dickinson, a nineteen-year-old bugler, was one of the few to survive the Alamo and afterwards went to Goliad.
kits: 這件長槍是西班牙方陣時代的兵器：十七世紀的長槍方陣與火槍隊配合使用，槍隊站在後排，長槍手擋在前面頂住騎兵衝鋒。它在德克薩斯革命裡的痕跡只剩兩處，而且都是餘緒。第一處在墨西哥軍隊：聖安納麾下的北方師與東方師仍保有槍騎兵團（Regimientos de Lanceros），騎手手中的長矛本質上就是架在馬背上的長槍，用來在遠距離上對付德克薩斯民兵與火槍隊，也是墨軍在聖哈辛托陣前唯一能與德克薩斯獵槍手比肩的衝鋒手段。第二處在聖安東尼奧：這座原為方濟各會傳教站的土坯堡壘沿用西班牙殖民時代的軍制與器械，守軍清冊裡仍留有少量舊式長槍與儀仗槍，3月6日夜間墨西哥軍分四縱隊攀牆時，守軍就是用斧、矛與獵刀在牆頭與院子裡迎戰。德克薩斯民兵這邊早已不配長槍：主力是德製燧發獵槍、滑膛燧發步槍、手槍與各式獵刀，寬背的布伊型獵刀在近身格鬥中比任何長柄兵器都管用。炮兵方面，德克薩斯方在聖安東尼奧有十八至二十四門砲，以四磅、六磅與十二磅為主，另有班·湯普森運來的兩門六磅砲雙生姊妹，以及那門寫著要拿就來拿的十八磅砲；從焚毀的縱帆船 San Felipe 上搶救下來的九磅砲 La Divina Pastora，則在聖哈辛托由湯姆·哈里斯少校使用。墨軍帶來的是十八磅與二十四磅攻城重砲，以牛車牽引，每天從千餘碼外轟擊。軍需方面，德克薩斯方的火藥與槍械多由美國商船運到墨西哥沿岸轉運，1835年一批價值可觀的軍火在格蘭德河口被墨西哥海關查獲扣押，成為決裂的導火線之一；聖安納的遠征軍自聖路易斯波托西步行約八百公里才抵達德克薩斯，途中已耗掉大量玉米、火藥與畜力。
kitsEn: This pike is a weapon of the Spanish square era: the pike block of the seventeenth century stood in front of the shot, holding off cavalry so that the musketeers could fire from the second rank. Only two traces of it survive in the Texas revolution, and both are survivals rather than uses. The first is in the Mexican army. Santa Anna's Department of the North and Department of the East still carried lancer regiments, Regimientos de Lanceros, and the lance those riders carried was in effect a pike mounted on horseback, used to reach the Texian militia and its musketeers at a distance and the only offensive weapon in the Mexican line that could stand up to the Texian hunting rifles at San Jacinto. The second is at San Antonio. The adobe compound, a converted Franciscan mission, kept the arms and ordinances of colonial Spanish service, and the garrison inventory still listed a small number of old pikes kept as guard and ceremonial weapons; when the Mexican columns scaled the wall on the night of 6 March, the defenders met them on the wall and in the courtyard with axes, pikes and hunting knives. The Texian militia had long since stopped carrying pikes altogether. Their strength lay in German-made flintlock hunting rifles, smoothbore flintlock muskets, pistols and every kind of hunting knife, and the heavy-bladed Bowie knife was more useful in a hand-to-hand struggle than any shafted weapon. In the artillery, the Texians at the Alamo had eighteen to twenty-four guns, mostly four, six and twelve pounders, together with the pair of six pounders known as the Twin Sisters that Ben Thompson brought up, and the eighteen pounder whose carriage bore the words Come and Take It. The nine pounder named La Divina Pastora, salvaged from the burning schooner San Felipe, was served at San Jacinto by Major Thomas H. Harris. On the Mexican side came eighteen and twenty-four pounder siege guns, hauled on ox carts and firing every day from more than a thousand yards. On the supply side, powder and small arms for the Texians came in American merchant ships and were transshipped along the Mexican coast; in 1835 a shipment of considerable value was seized and held by Mexican customs at the mouth of the Rio Grande, one of the sparks of the rupture. Santa Anna's expeditionary army walked some eight hundred kilometres from San Luis Potosí before it reached Texas, and had already burned through a great deal of corn, powder and draught animals on the way.
tactics: 德克薩斯方的戰術底子是拓荒者的散兵射擊。1835年10月2日岡薩拉斯之役，數百名德克薩斯民兵靠一座十八磅砲、拒馬與樹壘守住德薩克拉河橋頭，用散射與接近射擊把來犯的墨西哥營逐回東岸，讓德克薩斯第一次在陣地上取勝。隨後的貝克薩爾圍城（1835年11月下旬至12月9日）是一次典型的攻城示範：志願兵在夜裡用鐵鏟挖地道逼近方角堡的牆根，用迫近砲位壓制牆頭守軍，最後在砲火掩護下以梯隊強攻，奪回阿拉莫德帕拉斯堡壘，墨軍守軍趁夜棄城北撤，革命軍首度占領德克薩斯最重要的城市與軍械庫。1836年2月23日開始的聖安東尼奧圍城則是全戰役最殘酷的一段：墨軍以重砲每日轟擊，把土坯牆打得到處崩塌，再在3月6日夜裡以四路縱隊同時攀牆；守軍不足二百人，彈藥將盡，牆頭只剩斧頭與獵刀可以揮舞，堡壘在黎明前陷落。往後是全州性的崩解：古利亞德的守軍在三月被俘後遭槍殺，消息傳開，參加革命的各連隊與其眷屬沿鄉間道路向東退往布拉索斯河，軍隊與後方同時瓦解。休斯敦接手的則是相反的局面：他不追擊也不反攻，一面整頓新募的隊伍，一面用漁船與小艇自加爾維斯敦運來火藥、玉米與鹹豬肉，終於等到墨西哥主力在聖哈辛托河畔的一片樹林邊展開。四月二十一日，威廉·洛率九十人分隊先行奪下文斯河口的木橋，把墨軍增援堵在南岸，主力則利用天黑後潮水低平的淺灘渡過聖哈辛托河，一點四十五分從正面展開：德克薩斯軍以十二門砲先轟，再以密集散兵線前推，吶喊記住阿拉莫、記住古利亞德，墨軍陣形在十八分鐘內瓦解，總統聖安納在一株橡樹下被俘。
tacticsEn: The tactical base of the Texian side was the skirmish fire of frontiersmen. On 2 October 1835, at the first battle of Gonzales, several hundred Texian militia held the bridgehead over the De Witt colony creek with a single eighteen pounder, breastworks and felled timber, and drove the Mexican column back across the east bank with scattered volleys and close range shooting, giving Texas its first victory on a defended position. The siege of Béxar that followed, from late November to 9 December 1835, was a model demonstration of siege work: volunteers dug a trench toward the foot of the wall of the Alamo de Parras by night with spades, emplaced guns to silence the parapet, and at last went up the wall under cover of fire, taking the fort while the Mexican garrison withdrew north by night. For the first time the revolutionaries held the most important town and arsenal of Texas. The siege of San Antonio that began on 23 February 1836 was the cruelest passage of the whole war. The Mexican guns fired every day, the adobe walls were brought down in places, and on the night of 6 March four columns scaled the walls at once. Fewer than two hundred defenders remained, the ammunition was nearly spent, and on the parapet there was nothing to swing but axes and hunting knives. The fort fell before dawn. What followed was a collapse of the whole province: after the prisoners at Goliad were shot in March the news spread, the companies that had taken part in the revolt and their families withdrew east along the country roads towards the Brazos, and army and rear area came apart together. Houston inherited the opposite condition. He neither pursued nor counter-attacked; he drilled the newly raised companies while fishing boats and light craft carried powder, corn and salt pork up from Galveston, until the Mexican main force deployed on the edge of the woods along the San Jacinto river. On 21 April William Law took ninety men ahead to seize the wooden bridge over Vince's Bayou, shutting the Mexican reinforcements in on the south side, while the main body crossed the San Jacinto over the shallows on the ebb of a dark night. At a quarter to five the Texians deployed in the open: twelve guns first, then the skirmish line pressed forward shouting Remember the Alamo and Remember Goliad. The Mexican formation came apart in eighteen minutes, and the president was taken under an oak tree.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下，諸家史家在關鍵點上仍有出入，宜作概數看待。岡薩拉斯之役：德克薩斯守軍約一百八十人，墨西哥來犯部隊三百至六百人。貝克薩爾圍城：德克薩斯方志願兵約八百至一千人，加上堡內二百五十至三百名守軍；墨軍約一千五百至一千八百人；墨軍陣亡約二百五十人、被俘約三百五十人，德克薩斯方陣亡三十至五十人，其中多數死於12月7日的地道爆炸。聖安東尼奧圍城：守軍最終約一百八十至二百人，含3月1日突入的岡薩拉斯的32人；墨軍在阿拉莫周邊合計約五千至六千人，圍城歷時十三日；古利亞德方面3月27日被槍斃的俘虜約三百五十至四百人。聖哈辛托：休斯敦自報德克薩斯軍八百人，今人估計連民兵與後勤約一千八百至二千人；墨軍五千四百人，但真正投入戰鬥的約一千五百至一千八百人；交戰自一點四十五分起歷時十八分鐘；墨軍陣亡約六百五十人、受傷約七百三十人、被俘約一千二百人，德克薩斯軍陣亡九至十人、受傷約六十人。行程上，聖安納的大軍自聖路易斯波托西行軍約八百公里、耗時約六週才抵達德克薩斯；1835至36年間德克薩斯的歐裔移民定居者約二萬人，另有數萬特哈諾居民。時間線依次為：1835年3月首次公議會、10月2日岡薩拉斯、12月9日貝克薩爾、1836年2月23日圍城開始、3月2日獨立宣言、3月6日聖安東尼奧陷落、3月27日古利亞德、4月21日聖哈辛托、6月12日維爾卡索條約、9月共和國憲法。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run as follows, though historians differ at several key points and they should be read as approximations. At Gonzales the Texian garrison was about one hundred and eighty men against a Mexican force of three to six hundred. In the siege of Béxar the Texian volunteers numbered about eight hundred to a thousand, with two hundred and fifty to three hundred men of the garrison inside the walls, against fifteen hundred to eighteen hundred Mexicans; the Mexicans lost about two hundred and fifty dead and three hundred and fifty prisoners, the Texians thirty to fifty dead, most of them in the explosion of the mine on 7 December. In the siege of San Antonio the garrison finally numbered about one hundred and eighty to two hundred men, including the Thirty-Two of Gonzales who broke in on 1 March; the Mexicans had some five to six thousand around the Alamo, and the siege lasted thirteen days; at Goliad on 27 March some three hundred and fifty to four hundred prisoners were shot. At San Jacinto Houston's own figure for the Texian army was eight hundred men, and modern estimates counting militia and followers give one thousand eight hundred to two thousand; of Santa Anna's five thousand four hundred only some fifteen hundred to eighteen hundred were engaged; the action ran from a quarter to five for eighteen minutes; the Mexicans lost about six hundred and fifty dead, seven hundred and thirty wounded and twelve hundred prisoners, while the Texians lost nine or ten dead and about sixty wounded. On movement, Santa Anna's army marched some eight hundred kilometres from San Luis Potosí and took about six weeks to reach Texas; the European-descended settler population of Texas in 1835 and 1836 was about twenty thousand, with tens of thousands of Tejanos besides. The dates in order are: the first consultation, March 1835; Gonzales, 2 October; Béxar, 9 December; the opening of the siege of the Alamo, 23 February 1836; the Declaration of Independence, 2 March; the fall of the Alamo, 6 March; Goliad, 27 March; San Jacinto, 21 April; the Treaties of Velasco, 12 June; and the constitution of the republic in September.
cause: 開火的原因不是單一的。制度層面上，1834年墨西哥政府頒布關稅與撤廢德克薩斯自治的法令，把原本自治的科阿韋拉－德克薩斯州收歸中央，州議會被解散，移民自治的合法性被抽走，而德克薩斯的土地勘察、牧場焚燒與邊境掠奪又使農場主與政府之間的怨恨日積月累。軍事層面上，聖安納執政後要向全國證明自己對邊疆強硬，於是把原本駐在聖路易斯波托西的部隊調回德克薩斯，勒令地方武裝繳械，又派遣規模遠超實際需要的遠征軍北上。具體導火線有三：1834年的波爾克信要求墨西哥當局交還被扣留的舊陸軍，聖安納的答覆近乎最後通牒；1835年德克薩斯方面購置的一批槍械火藥在格蘭德河口被墨西哥海關查獲扣押；州總督佩雷斯被召回、軍方與居民對立公開化。於是邊境上的私人暴力迅速累積，規模從十幾人的武裝巡邏發展成上千人的志願軍，法律秩序在墨西哥大軍集結之前就已失效。德克薩斯的人口以德意志裔為主，革命方的募兵辦法、組織方式與政治語言都帶著美國西部拓荒地的特徵，這也解釋了為何革命一方始終把鬥爭訴諸美國式的憲法、選舉與民兵制度，而不是殖民地式的請願。
causeEn: There was no single cause. On the level of institutions, in 1834 the Mexican government issued its tariff decrees and abolished the self-government of Texas, pulling the state of Coahuila and Texas back under the centre, dissolving the state assembly and removing the legal basis of settler autonomy; and in Texas the surveying of land, the burning of ranches and the raiding of the frontier piled grievances up between the farmers and the government. On the military level, Santa Anna needed to show the whole country that he was hard on the frontier once he was back in power, so he moved troops that had been stationed at San Luis Potosí back into Texas, ordered the local armed bands to surrender their weapons, and sent north an expeditionary army far larger than the situation required. There were three concrete sparks: the Polk letter of 1834 demanding that the Mexican authorities hand back the old garrison troops that had been held, which Santa Anna's answer turned into something close to an ultimatum; the seizure in 1835 by Mexican customs of a consignment of arms and powder bought by the Texians at the mouth of the Rio Grande; and the recall of Governor Pérez together with the open enmity between the soldiers and the settlers. From there the private violence of the border accumulated quickly, growing from armed patrols of a dozen men to volunteer companies of a thousand, and legal order had already collapsed before the Mexican army assembled. The population of Texas was predominantly German-descended, and the recruitment, the organisation and the political language of the revolutionaries all carried the marks of the American frontier, which is why they argued the case in the idiom of American constitutions, elections and militia rather than in that of colonial petition.
impact: 革命的直接後果是德克薩斯共和國的建立。1836年3月2日，華盛頓－布拉索斯河畔的公議會通過獨立宣言；9月的憲法確立了總統、兩院議會與最高法院，規定奴隸制度暫時保留，同時以移民法規把公民權與選舉權限制在德裔與少數合格者手中，這套制度一直用到德克薩斯於1845年加入美國、1865年廢奴之後才被逐步推翻。共和國的存在也把聖安納身後的集團推向戰爭：1836年6月的維爾卡索條約承認德克薩斯獨立，墨西哥在屈辱中被迫承認德國出生的弗里德里希·艾內克為德克薩斯總統，更激化了德國出生者是否真的忠於墨西哥的猜疑。1846至1848年的美墨戰爭使德克薩斯成為美軍進軍墨西哥的後方基地，戰後的瓜達盧普－伊達爾戈條約確認了德克薩斯的邊界。長期來看，這場革命把拓荒者的自治神話寫進了美國西部的政治想像：要拿就來拿的旗，記住阿拉莫、記住古利亞德的吶喊，成為後來美國人在海外介入時反覆引用的口號；德克薩斯也自此在美國擴張史上佔據一個特殊位置。反過來，對墨西哥而言，這是十九世紀國家主義最痛的一次挫敗：德克薩斯一地的居民數與兵力都遠小於墨西哥全國，卻因訓練、補給與指揮的全線差距而失去整個北部邊疆，迫使墨西哥此後改革軍制，廢除殖民時代的民兵編制而建立職業軍。
impactEn: The direct consequence of the revolution was the founding of the Republic of Texas. On 2 March 1836 the consultation at Washington-on-the-Brazos adopted the Declaration of Independence, and the constitution of September set up a president, a bicameral legislature and a supreme court, kept slavery in place for the time being and at the same time limited citizenship and the franchise through its immigration law to a German-descended and otherwise qualified minority; that settlement lasted until Texas entered the Union in 1845 and slavery was abolished in 1865, and was only then dismantled piece by piece. The existence of the republic also drove Santa Anna's own faction towards war: the Treaties of Velasco of June 1836 recognised independent Texas, and Mexico in humiliation had to accept a German-born man, Friedrich von Ernst, as president of Texas, which sharpened the suspicion that German-born subjects were not really loyal to Mexico. The Mexican-American war of 1846 to 1848 turned Texas into the rear base for an American invasion of Mexico, and the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo afterwards fixed its boundaries. In the long run the revolution wrote the myth of frontier self-government into the political imagination of the American west: the Come and Take It flag and the cry of Remember the Alamo and Remember Goliad became the formulas later Americans quoted whenever they intervened abroad, and Texas has held a peculiar place in the story of American expansion ever since. The other way round, for Mexico this was the most painful blow to national pride in the nineteenth century. The inhabitants and the armed strength of Texas were a fraction of those of Mexico as a whole, yet through an across-the-board failure of training, supply and command the whole northern frontier was lost, and Mexico was driven afterwards to reform its army, to strike out the colonial militia system and to build a professional force.
result: 結果是德克薩斯獨立、墨西哥軍隊退出德州。1836年4月21日聖哈辛托一戰，德克薩斯軍以不足一千人的兵力，在十八分鐘內打垮墨西哥陸軍最精銳的一支，陣亡與被俘合計逾二千人，總統安東尼奧·洛佩斯·德·聖安納本人在營地附近的一株橡樹下被找到，次日成為俘虜；德克薩斯軍的代價是十人上下陣亡、六十人左右受傷。墨軍在德州北部的部隊與後方單位隨即潰散，聖安納回到墨西哥即被視為喪國之君，1836年6月被自己的部下推翻。翌年6月，休斯敦召集公議會制定憲法，德克薩斯共和國成立，國旗是白地單星的伯內特旗，首都在哥倫比亞，一八三七年遷至聖哈辛托，一八三九年再遷往以斯蒂芬·奧斯汀命名的奧斯汀。1845年美國吞併德克薩斯，1846至48年的美墨戰爭使這條邊界固化，1870年德克薩斯在廢奴之後重新加入聯邦，1876年另訂憲法恢復各項權利。德克薩斯革命由此成為少數以武力建立、以條約承認、又以國家身分被併入更大聯邦的完整案例：它贏得了自己的國家，卻沒能保住這個國家的主權。
resultEn: The result was the independence of Texas and the withdrawal of the Mexican army from the province. At San Jacinto on 21 April 1836 the Texian army, fewer than a thousand strong, broke the finest troops of the Mexican land army in eighteen minutes, with more than two thousand of the enemy dead or captured, and President Antonio López de Santa Anna himself was found under an oak tree near the camp and was a prisoner the following day; the Texian cost was some ten dead and about sixty wounded. The Mexican units in the north of the province and the rear services broke up at once, and Santa Anna went back to Mexico branded as the man who had lost the country, to be thrown out by his own officers in June 1836. In June of the following year Houston called a consultation that drew up a constitution, and the Republic of Texas came into being with a white single star flag, the Burnet flag; its capital was at Columbia, moved to Houston in 1837 and again to Austin in 1839, the town named for Stephen F. Austin. The United States annexed Texas in 1845, the Mexican-American war of 1846 to 48 fixed that frontier, and in 1870, after the abolition of slavery, Texas was readmitted to the Union, with a new constitution in 1876 restoring its rights. The Texas revolution is therefore one of the few complete cases in which a state was created by force, acknowledged by treaty and then absorbed into a larger union as a nation in its own right: it won itself a country and did not manage to keep that country's sovereignty.
